page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 6 physical cores and 12 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled, backed by a 35 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. Memory capacity totals 24 GB, presenting a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators, while delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent average-tier multi-threaded performance. The instance registers a PassMark CPU score of 11,934.41 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,894, complemented by a Clang compilation metric of 9,437. In memory benchmarks, large uncached read operations achieve 71.19 GB/s and writes achieve 42.85 GB/s. Network and caching efficiency is reflected in throughput tests, sustaining 10.16 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.0 GB/s in static web serving. Conversely, single-threaded processing exhibits lower relative throughput, with stress-ng single-core and compression tests (such as gzip and bzip3 decompression) placing in lower benchmark brackets.

The 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio offers an efficient resource balance for workloads prioritizing core density over expansive memory footprints. Because local NVMe storage is omitted, persistence depends entirely on network block storage. This profile suits multi-threaded batch processing, software compilation pipelines, microservices architectures, and horizontally scaled web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores alongside 24 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance features vector acceleration support through AVX-512 and VNNI, but does not include integrated local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and providing a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. In synthetic benchmarks, multi-core execution falls comfortably within mid-tier brackets, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,894 and steady software compilation metrics, whereas single-threaded throughput shows weaker relative rankings. With 10.16 million Redis operations per second and 9.0 GB/s static web throughput, it represents a cost-effective platform for compute-bound parallel workloads, microservice hosting, software build runners, and clustered web applications that operate efficiently within standard memory profiles.
